question: When choosing work, should you follow a passion you already have?
answer: Yes. Work fills most waking hours, and people who see their job as a calling report more satisfaction with work and with life. Knowing what absorbs you is real information about where you will put in the long effort that skill needs. Setting a strong interest aside to chase pay or prestige is a common regret.
move: Whichever side you took, the hinge is whether interest comes before skill or after.
ask: Which of my interests began only after I got good at something?
counterpoint: No. O'Keefe, Dweck and Walton found that people who believe passions are found, not developed, expect a true interest to bring endless motivation, and lose interest when the subject gets hard. Many people's passions grew out of work they first became good at. Waiting to discover a passion can mean never building one.
source: O'Keefe, Dweck and Walton, Psychological Science, 2018
reference: O'Keefe, Dweck and Walton, Implicit Theories of Interest: Finding Your Passion or Developing It?, Psychological Science, 2018
